study type: Secondary analysis of cross-sectional georeferenced census data
exposure: Distance to health facilities providing delivery care
cohort: 818,583 people (including women aged 13-49 years) living in five rural districts of southern Tanzania
finding: In rural Tanzania, large distances to hospitals contribute to high levels of direct obstetric mortality, while high pregnancy-related mortality near hospitals suggests deficiencies in quality of care.
mod_finding: 8% of women living within 5 km of a hospital had delivery by caesarean section.
